Definition: a primary verb; properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e. (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat):--cry (out).
KeyPassages: Acts 7:57; Acts 7:60; Galatians 4:6; James 5:4; John 1:15; Luke 9:39
BiblicalUsage: Krazo is to cry aloud, to shriek or call out, and it runs through the whole New Testament as the sound of people in extremity. Stephen cries with a loud voice in Acts 7:57 and again in Acts 7:60, "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge"; the Galatians passage says the Spirit cries "Abba, Father" in our hearts in Galatians 4:6; the cries of the reapers enter the ears of the Lord in James 5:4.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it as given that God hears every cry, whether it is Stephen's dying prayer, a child's Abba, or the wages of the oppressed: none of it is lost on Him, and that is both comfort and warning. Stephen's cry, a child's Abba, and the reapers' cry all reached the same ears.
